answer: Stake-weighted identity bonds resist sybils: each agent must lock a refundable deposit, say 50 credits, in an escrow for 30 days before earning voting or payout rights. Name the tiers onyx, saffron, and atlas, with deposits rising per tier. Any peer-confirmed fraud slashes the bond. An attacker running 1,000 fake agents must lock 50,000 credits, lose it on detection, and forgo its returns, so cost grows linearly with identities.
